newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Europ Assistance to launch S.Africa AIDS insurance.
newsitem.headline: Europ Assistance to launch S.Africa AIDS insurance.

text.p: The South African unit of Europ Assistance said on Wednesday it would announce details of a range of fully-reinsured HIV/AIDS insurance products in March.

A spokeswoman for Europ Assistance said the product range, to be called Euro Q Care+, would consist of three differentiated products, some of which would cater for patients who had already contracted HIV/AIDS and others for people who were virus-free.
The company gave no further details but said in a statement the products would be suited for inclusion in medical schemes and life insurance portfolios.

"We believe our new products will provide specific and significant benefits and treatment protocols, as well as protecting individuals whose daily lives expose them to risk," Lisa Volker, group medical underwriter, said in the statement.

HIV/AIDS insurance products are already available in South Africa. Policies are generally split into two categories, catering firstly for people who can prove they are virus-free and secondly for those testing positive.
Figures vary, but about four percent of South Africa's population, or 1.5 million people, are estimated to be already infected with the AIDS virus and levels will rise in the years to come.
Volker said although premiums on the Europ Assistance products would be low they would be dependent on the infection risk rating given to each independent scheme.
"We will consider tailoring managed health benefit programmes for existing members who are known HIV/AIDS sufferers, in consultation with the scheme or employer," Volker said.
